      <h1 class="page-title">My Journey</h1>
      <p class="about-hook-text">I’m drawn to the moment a pattern starts to explain a decision. Before studying analytics formally, I was already using customer behaviour, revenue and team performance in commercial roles to ask a practical question: what is the evidence telling me?</p>
    </div>

    <section class="journey">

      <div class="stage">
        <span class="stage-marker"></span>
        <div class="stage-body">
          <h2 class="stage-title">Commercial leadership and judgement</h2>
          <p class="stage-meta">TigerWit · Business Development Manager</p>
          <p class="stage-text">At TigerWit, I used customer, CRM and conversion information to guide acquisition and revenue decisions. I led a five-person team and improved sales KPI results by <span class="data">40%</span>. I learned to look beyond activity counts and ask what they revealed about customer engagement and business performance.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="stage">
        <span class="stage-marker"></span>
        <div class="stage-body">
          <h2 class="stage-title">Business Analytics</h2>
          <p class="stage-meta">MSc Management with Business Analytics · Bournemouth University · Merit</p>
          <p class="stage-text">I completed my MSc to add stronger analytical methods to the commercial judgement I had developed in practice. I learned to test results carefully and explain what the evidence can, and cannot, support.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="stage">
        <span class="stage-marker"></span>
        <div class="stage-body">
          <h2 class="stage-title">Analytics in practice</h2>
          <p class="stage-meta">7+ years across commercial and operational roles<br />SQL · Power BI · Excel · R</p>
          <p class="stage-text">I use SQL, Power BI, Excel and R to structure questions, validate results and communicate evidence. My WERS project examines how reward and workplace factors are associated with job satisfaction, while making limitations clear.</p>

  <section class="brings">
      <p class="brings-intro">The work I enjoy most sits in that middle space: listening to what the business is struggling with, finding the evidence underneath it, and turning it into something people can actually use.</p>

      <div class="brings-grid">
        <div class="bring-card">

          <h3 class="bring-title">SQL &amp; Validation</h3>
          <p class="bring-text">Reconciliation, data-quality investigation and cross-tool checks. In my WERS project, 22 independent SQL validation checks passed, with a maximum difference between R and SQL of <span class="data">0.005</span>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="bring-card">

          <p class="bring-text">Weighted descriptive analysis, regression and decision-tree sensitivity analysis, with interpretation matched to the data.</p>
